item.title: GAA agree to allow Ireland use Páirc Uí Chaoimh
item.description: The GAA have agreed to allow the Republic of Ireland women's team to use SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh this summer. The soccer team play the Netherlands in a women’s World Cup qualifier on the 5th of June. Meanwhile Central Council has also given permission for Derry City to use GAA venue Celtic Park in April and May of this year. Advertisement The Candystripes will need a temporary home as a new hybrid pitch will be installed at the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium.

item.title: Vital win for West Ham
item.description: West Ham have moved to within two points of safety with a dramatic 3-1 win at home to Sunderland in the Premier League. Manchester City can cut Arsenal's lead to four points if they can get their first top flight victory of 2026 at home to bottom club Wolves. In the Championship there have been big wins for promotion-chasing teams in the early matches. Advertisement Second placed Middlesbrough are 3 points off leaders Coventry after beating Preston 4-nil. item.title: Tralee into Corn Ui Mhuiri final but Milltown out
item.description: Tralee CBS have won their Corn Ui Mhuiri semi-final, registering a 1-15 to 7 points victory over St Francis College Rochestown. Tralee led 1-9 to 0-4 at half time. Presentation Secondary School Milltown lost to Clonmel High School, who won 1-10 to 1-8. Milltown were in front by 1-8 to 0-5 at half time. Advertisement

item.title: Straight sets win for Djokovic
item.description: Novak Djokovic got a straight-sets victory over Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp to reach the fourth round of the Australian Open. It was his 400th Grand Slam win. But Djokovic was lucky not to be disqualified in the second set after showing his frustration and nearly hitting a ball girl. Advertisement There were also wins today for Jannick Sinner, Caspur Ruud and Blake Shelton. Iga Swiatek, Elina Rybakina and Amanda Anisimova all safely made it through to the next round of the women's draw.

item.title: Kingdom win at Dublin
item.description: Kerry were victorious at Dublin in the opening round of the Lidl Ladies Nation Football League. The Division 1 encounter at Round Towers ended 2-9 to 0-9 in favour of the Kingdom. Advertisement Jadyn Lucey and Mary O’Connell struck crucial goals at a rain-soaked JYSK Park in Clondalkin on Saturday afternoon as title holders Kerry kick-started their Lidl National Football League Division 1 campaign with victory over All-Ireland SFC champions Dublin. item.title: Man City defeat Wolves
item.description: Manchester City have cut Arsenal's lead at the top of the Premier League to 4 points. City beat bottom club Wolves 2-nil with both goals before the break. Tottenham were held 2-2 at relegation-threatened Burnley. Advertisement Improving West Ham made it back -to-back wins with a 3-1 victory at home to Sunderland at lunchtime. Fulham came from behind and won 2-1 against Brighton.

item.title: Ulster beaten
item.description: Ulster look set to fall out of the URC's top four. Richie Murphy's men let a late lead slip as they fell to a 27-22 defeat away at the Scarlets. Advertisement
